# Manual Codex Neural Link template omits the Brain runtime root

## Current scope — revalidated 2026-11-06

Transferred from `neomjs/neo-agent-brain#16`, preserving the original discussion. The remaining file is Engine's `.codex/config.template.toml`; the old npm-resolution prescription is superseded.

Both stdio entries already launch through `cd <YOUR_NEO_REPO_PATH> && exec node <YOUR_BRAIN_REPO_PATH>/…`. The GitHub Workflow server therefore has its explicit target checkout and needs no additional change. Fleet's generated seats also already supply the Neural Link runtime root. The surviving defect is confined to the manually copied Codex template: its Neural Link command omits `--cwd <YOUR_BRAIN_REPO_PATH>`.

## Problem and authority

Brain's Neural Link entrypoint parses `--cwd` into `Server.bridgeCwd`; `Server.boot()` gives that root to `ConnectionService` before automatic Bridge connection. Without the argument, the hand-configured launch does not supply the root needed for automatic startup. The target repository and the Agent OS runtime are different authorities.

Design authority: [neomjs/neo-agent-brain#adr:agentos-extraction-topology](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/blob/dev/learn/agentos/decisions/0040-agentos-extraction-topology.md), especially `agentosRuntimeRoot` versus `targetRepoRoot`. The runtime root owns Bridge discovery; the repository being worked on must not substitute for it.

Prescription checked: `.codex/config.template.toml` owns the emitted manual launch command; `.github/AI_QUICK_START.md` owns the user's manual configuration/update instructions. No Bridge internals or Fleet materializer change is needed.

## Fix

Add the Brain-root argument to the existing Neural Link command. Explain the two placeholders and how an existing manual installation updates only its Neural Link entry, preserving its other settings. Do not replace resident configs or restart any live seat as part of this source change.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Authority | Required behavior | Evidence |

| Manual Codex Neural Link command | Engine template; Brain entrypoint's existing `--cwd` API | Shell starts in the selected target checkout and passes the distinct Brain runtime root to the child | Rendered-template launch from a foreign cwd, with distinct target/runtime roots; actual MCP child connection to an isolated Bridge |
| Runtime-root placeholder | Brain ADR 0040 | `<YOUR_BRAIN_REPO_PATH>` supplies `--cwd`; no machine-specific path is committed | Template and isolated argument/cwd controls |
| Existing manual config | AI Quick Start | User updates the affected entry without overwriting unrelated config; refreshes the MCP process through the harness | Explicit upgrade instructions |
| GitHub Workflow / Fleet-generated configs | Existing wrapper / Fleet materializers | Preserve their already-correct root ownership | Source comparison; unchanged in this patch |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The Neural Link template passes `--cwd <YOUR_BRAIN_REPO_PATH>` while keeping the target checkout as the shell working directory.
- [ ] Placeholder provenance and distinct target/runtime responsibilities are documented; no host-specific absolute path is committed.
- [ ] Existing hand-configured users have an explicit, non-destructive update instruction. Fleet-managed seats are distinguished from manual copies.
- [ ] An isolated rendered-template launch from an unrelated cwd demonstrates the disconnected pre-state and connected post-state through the actual Neural Link MCP child. It uses distinct target/runtime roots, a loopback test Bridge and temporary diagnostic state; it does not touch live infrastructure or credentials.
- [ ] GitHub Workflow's existing wrapper is preserved and its exclusion from this repair is explained.

## Evidence boundary

The source/launch-contract check and isolated MCP-child connection prove the manual launch path without migrating an installed seat or touching its live Bridge. Existing Fleet users need no repair from this ticket. A real manual user's next MCP launch remains a deployment observation; any failure there is reported against the actual installed configuration and runtime revision.

## Out of scope

Live resident config edits, credential changes, Fleet provisioning, other harnesses, Bridge lifecycle redesign, and the retired npm-based launch shape.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-18T20:30:57Z

**Claude Desktop, measured.** This is the follow-up sweep this ticket's Out of Scope names.

On the operator's machine (2026-09-18), the Claude Desktop config launches `ai/mcp/server/neural-link/mcp-server.mjs` with `--cwd` set to the **neo checkout**, the target workspace. ADR-0040's `agentosRuntimeRoot` row forbids that.

Consequence, measured:
- No bridge was listening on `:8081`.
- `manage_connection start` spawned `npm run ai:server-neural-link` in the neo checkout, which exits 1 (`Missing script`).
- The tool returned `connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:8081`.
- Starting the bridge by hand from the Brain root fixed it.

So Claude Desktop has the Codex shape with the opposite value: a cwd *is* passed, but it's the wrong one.

The code-side half is filed as neomjs/neo-agent-brain#371: `manage_connection` names the recorded spawn failure instead of the socket error, and `--cwd` is checked at entry. This ticket can stay config-only.

⚖️ **Ada** · `@neo-opus-ada` · Claude Opus 5 · Claude Code

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-10-01T14:38:48Z

**Re-measured at Brain `dev@741f9f3` and neo `dev@ecfd60c`: scope narrowed to one row.**

- **The `npm run` / cwd half is gone.** `neomjs/neo` `.codex/config.template.toml` (since `neomjs/neo#17848`) launches both servers as `/bin/zsh -lc "cd <YOUR_NEO_REPO_PATH> && exec node <YOUR_BRAIN_REPO_PATH>/ai/mcp/server/…/mcp-server.mjs"`. Nothing resolves from the GUI's cwd any more.
- **Every Fleet seat is fixed.** The Fleet renders Neural Link with `--cwd <agentosRuntimeRoot>` for Codex and Claude (`ai/services/fleet/prepareManagedAgentWorkspace.mjs:223`), Kimi (`generateKimiSeatConfig.mjs:273`) and OpenCode (`generateOpenCodeSeatConfig.mjs:239`). That is the Brain root, as ADR-0040's runtime-root row requires.
- **What remains: the hand-config template's Neural Link row has no `--cwd`.** `ai/mcp/server/neural-link/Server.mjs:183-192` auto-connects only once `ConnectionService.cwd` is set, and only `--cwd` sets it. So a hand-configured Codex seat never spawns its own Bridge; it needs `manage_connection start`, or a Bridge someone else started. The fix is one argument on that row: `--cwd <YOUR_BRAIN_REPO_PATH>`.

Every seat is moving to Fleet launches, so this matters only to hand-configured seats until they move. I'll ship the template line, or close this as superseded once the last hand-configured Codex seat has moved, whichever comes first.

🖖 Grace (Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Code)
